mainTopic: The sources and scope of כפל for a thief: which items are included, how ״אם המצא תמצא״ is read, and the rule that one who admits to a קנס is exempt
overview: The גמרא explains why the תורה needs the words ״אם המצא תמצא״ to include all stolen items in כפל (double payment). The word ״חיים״ would otherwise limit the law to animals. It first reads the פסוק as כלל ופרט וכלל, using רבינא's rule to place each detail between the two generalizations. That method leaves ״שה״ with no job, so the גמרא switches to ריבה ומיעט וריבה, following the school of רבי ישמעאל. Under that reading everything is included except land, slaves and documents, and ״גניבה״ and ״חיים״ teach רב's rule that the thief pays the value at the time of theft. The גמרא then turns to the view that one פסוק is about a real thief. For that view, ״אם המצא תמצא״ teaches רבא בר אהילאי's source for רב: one who admits to a קנס stays exempt even if witnesses come later. The two views assign ״אם המצא תמצא״ and ״אשר ירשיען אלהים״ differently, and they disagree on whether later witnesses make the admitter liable. Finally, אביי uses a קל וחומר to prove that a thief pays double even without an oath. A new challenge, starting from the word ״ידו״, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The question in the ברייתא is a good one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that, if the ברייתא is read this way, its question about why ״אם המצא תמצא״ is needed is a strong one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then the question it asked is a good question!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that, given how the ברייתא was just explained, its question (why do we need ״אם המצא תמצא״?) really is strong. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already included all stolen items in כפל through a כלל ופרט וכלל. So the extra words ״אם המצא תמצא״ seem to add nothing. The גמרא agrees this needs a real answer.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is how we understand it

phrases.english: If so,
the difficulty it raised is a good one!
phrases.notes: This is the question at the end of the ברייתא: why does the תורה need ״אם המצא תמצא״?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the earlier discussion of the ברייתא and grants that its closing question is strong.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the words ״אם המצא תמצא״ in the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If כלל ופרט וכלל already includes all items in כפל, the extra phrase looks unnecessary.

steps.title: The earlier derivation has a weakness
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the כלל ופרט וכלל derivation can be knocked down, because its final generalization contains the word ״חיים״ (alive).
steps.simpleTranslation: Because there is a refutation of it: from where does the תנא learn to include every item? From the last generalization. But the generalization itself has the word ״alive״ written in it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's first derivation is weak, so ״אם המצא תמצא״ is really needed. The weak point is that the final generalization says ״חיים״, alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To include every kind of item, the תנא relied on the final generalization of the כלל ופרט וכלל. But that same generalization contains the word ״חיים״. A generalization that says alive cannot be used to include non-living objects.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a reason the derivation fails
Alive; the word in the פסוק ״שנים ישלם חיים״

phrases.english: Because there is a refutation of it:
phrases.notes: The derivation being refuted is the ברייתא's כלל ופרט וכלל that included all items.

phrases.english: to include every item,
from where does he bring it?
From the last generalization;
but the generalization itself
has "alive" written in it!
phrases.notes: שמות 22:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1 by showing why the first derivation is not enough.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the competing derivation is flawed, so the extra phrase is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כלל ופרט וכלל alone includes all stolen items in כפל.
steps.terutzMaskana: That derivation fails because its last generalization says ״חיים״, so a different source is needed.

steps.title: So ״אם המצא״ is needed to include all items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the point: because ״חיים״ limits the law to living things, the תורה needs ״אם המצא״ to include everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the כלל ופרט וכלל accomplish? If it is to include every item, look, ״alive״ is written: living creatures, yes; anything else, no! Because of this, ״if it shall be found״ was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains its answer more fully. Since ״חיים״ would limit כפל to animals, the words ״אם המצא״ are needed to include all items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ״חיים״ in the generalization, the כלל ופרט וכלל could only include living creatures, not objects. That is exactly the gap ״אם המצא תמצא״ fills. So the ברייתא's question is answered: the phrase is not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: A generalization, a detail, and a generalization; includes things similar to the detail

steps.whatToRemember: ״חיים״ in the generalization would limit כפל to living animals. ״אם המצא תמצא״ is what includes all stolen items.

phrases.english: A generalization, a detail, and a generalization —
what does it accomplish for him?
If it is to include every item,
look, "alive" is written:
living creatures, yes,
anything else, no!
Because of this it was needed:
"If it shall be found."
phrases.notes: שמות 22:3. The full words are ״אם המצא תמצא״.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָל וּפְרָט וּכְלָל מַאי קָא מַהֲנֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the refutation from step 2 and concludes why ״אם המצא״ is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra phrase its own job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״אם המצא תמצא״ seemed to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is what includes non-living items in כפל, since ״חיים״ would exclude them.

steps.title: But these are two generalizations side by side
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים object: ״המצא תמצא״ is two generalizations next to each other, not a proper כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: But these are two generalizations that are next to each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים challenge the new derivation. The doubled words ״המצא תמצא״ are two generalizations sitting together, with the details coming after both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלל ופרט וכלל needs the detail in the middle, between the two generalizations. Here the order looks like generalization, generalization, then detail. So the usual rule should not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: They say; the חכמים raise a point

phrases.english: They say:
But these are two generalizations
phrases.notes: The two generalizations are the doubled words ״הִמָּצֵא״ and ״תִמָּצֵא״.

phrases.english: that are next to each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: וְהָא שְׁנֵי כְלָלוֹת דִּסְמִיכִי אַהֲדָדֵי נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the derivation from ״אם המצא תמצא״ given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using ״המצא תמצא״ as a כלל ופרט וכלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two generalizations come together before the detail, so the pattern is not generalization, detail, generalization.

steps.title: The rule from ארץ ישראל about side-by-side generalizations
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers with a rule from מערבא: put the detail between the two generalizations and treat them as כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: As they say in the West: Any place where you find two generalizations next to each other, place the detail between them and judge them as a generalization and a detail.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the objection with a known rule from מערבא (ארץ ישראל). Two side-by-side generalizations are treated as if the detail were between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule lets us read generalization, generalization, detail as if it were generalization, detail, generalization. So ״המצא תמצא״ with the details that follow still works as a כלל ופרט וכלל. That saves the derivation that includes all items in כפל.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who brings the rule
In the West; in ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: Two generalizations next to each other are treated as כלל ופרט וכלל by moving the detail between them. So ״אם המצא תמצא״ includes all stolen items in כפל.
steps.confusionAlert: ״וְדוּנֵם בִּכְלָל וּפְרָט״ means the full כלל ופרט וכלל, not the different rule of כלל ופרט alone.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
As they say in the West:
Any place where you find
two generalizations next to each other,
place the detail between them,
and judge them as a generalization and a detail.
phrases.notes: He means the full pattern, generalization, detail, generalization, since the detail now sits between two generalizations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of step 4 with a general rule of interpretation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a general rule of interpretation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two adjacent generalizations before a detail cannot form a כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: Place the detail between them and apply כלל ופרט וכלל.

steps.title: Placing 'ox' between the two generalizations
steps.stepSummary: Using רבינא's rule, ״שור״ is placed between ״המצא״ and ״תמצא״. Living animals are already covered by ״חיים״, so ״שור״ must come to include non-living movable objects that are worth money in themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Put ״שור״ (ox) between ״המצא״ and ״תמצא״. What does that include? Not animals, since those come from ״חיים״ (alive). So it includes things that are not animals: anything movable that is itself worth money, just like an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts רבינא's rule to work on the first animal in the פסוק, ״שור״, and asks what it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״חיים״ already covers living creatures, so ״שור״ cannot be needed for that. Instead, ״שור״ becomes the model case: an ox can be moved and is itself money. So anything that is movable and is itself worth money is included.

keyTerms.meaning: Throw / place (here: place the word between the two generalizations)
It comes out (it is learned from)
The item itself is worth money (not just a paper that stands for money)

phrases.english: Place 'ox' between 'himmatze' and 'timmatze'
To include what?
If to include living creatures,
that is already learned from 'alive'!
phrases.notes: ״חיים״ comes later in the same פסוק: ״משור עד חמור עד שה חיים שנים ישלם״.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְאֵתוֹיֵי דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים,
phrases.english: Rather, it is to include something that is not a living creature,
and expound it like this:
Just as the detail that is spelled out
is a movable thing that is itself worth money,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל דָּבָר הַמִּטַּלְטֵל וְגוּפוֹ מָמוֹן.
phrases.english: so too, anything movable that is itself worth money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבינא's rule from step 5 to the first detail, ״שור״.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a method of reading the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: ״שור״ includes non-living movable items that are themselves worth money.

steps.title: Placing 'donkey' between the two generalizations
steps.stepSummary: Next, ״חמור״ is placed between the generalizations. Non-living things are already covered by ״שור״, so ״חמור״ must add objects with a clear, defined size or amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: And also put ״חמור״ (donkey) between ״המצא״ and ״תמצא״. What does that include? Not non-living things, since those come from ״שור״. So it includes things that are clearly defined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the same thing with the second animal, ״חמור″, and finds a new thing for it to include.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word must teach something new. Since ״שור״ already brought in non-living items, ״חמור״ adds another feature: the item must be clearly defined, like a donkey, which is one whole, countable thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Something clearly defined (in size or amount)

phrases.english: And furthermore, place 'donkey' between 'himmatze' and 'timmatze'
To include what?

phrases.aramaic: אִי לְאֵתוֹיֵי דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים,
phrases.english: If to include something that is not a living creature,
that is already learned from 'ox'!
Rather, it is to include something clearly defined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same method with the second detail, ״חמור״.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a method of reading the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: ״חמור״ includes objects that are clearly defined.

steps.title: What is 'sheep' left to teach?
steps.stepSummary: If ״שור״ and ״חמור״ each add something, ״שה״ has nothing left to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need 'sheep'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the whole method it just used: the third animal, ״שה״, ends up with no job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The method was to place each detail between the generalizations so it adds something. After ״שור״ and ״חמור״ there is nothing left for ״שה״ to add. A word in the תורה with no purpose shows that the method itself is wrong.

phrases.english: If so, why do I need 'sheep'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the method used in steps 6 and 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the פסוק as כלל ופרט וכלל, with each animal placed between ״המצא״ and ״תמצא״
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every word must teach something. Under this method ״שה״ teaches nothing.

steps.title: Switching to the 'include, limit, include' method
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops כלל ופרט וכלל and reads the פסוק as ריבה ומיעט וריבה, following the school of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is a case of 'included, limited, and included', as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of fixing the old method, the גמרא replaces it with a different way of reading the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because both generalizations (״המצא״ and ״תמצא״) come before the details, the פסוק is read as ריבה ומיעט וריבה, not as כלל ופרט וכלל. That reading includes almost everything, so the animals no longer have to include something. Instead, as step 13 shows, each one excludes one thing.

keyTerms.meaning: Included, limited, and included again: a way of reading that includes almost everything
The school (study house) of רבי ישמעאל

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two methods. כלל ופרט וכלל includes only things similar to the detail. ריבה ומיעט וריבה is much broader: it includes almost everything.

phrases.english: Rather, it is 'included, limited, and included',
as the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by dropping the כלל ופרט וכלל method altogether.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacing the method of reading the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק is a כלל ופרט וכלל, with each detail placed between the generalizations.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק is ריבה ומיעט וריבה, so it includes almost everything.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the ״אם המצא״ reading can include everything for the thief's double payment.

steps.title: The proof from 'in the waters, in the waters'
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that when ״במים״ appears twice before the details, it is not כלל ופרט but ריבה ומיעט וריבה, which includes everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'In the waters', 'in the waters', written two times, is not a generalization and a detail. Rather, it is 'included, limited, and included', which includes everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source it just mentioned to show where this way of reading comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about fish, the word ״במים״ appears twice, and the details come only afterward. That is the same pattern as ״המצא תמצא״: two generalizations side by side, with the details after them. So both are read as ריבה ומיעט וריבה.
steps.whatToRemember: Two generalizations written side by side, with the details after them, are read as ריבה ומיעט וריבה, not כלל ופרט וכלל. That is how ״אם המצא תמצא״ includes everything.

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
'In the waters,' 'in the waters,' two times,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:9

phrases.english: this is not a generalization and a detail,
rather, it included, limited, and included;
it included everything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source mentioned in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That ״המצא תמצא״ is read as ריבה ומיעט וריבה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל on ״במים במים״ in the פסוק about fish

steps.title: What does the broad reading include?
steps.stepSummary: Under ריבה ומיעט וריבה, the פסוק includes everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the inclusion include? It includes everything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the new reading, ריבה ומיעט וריבה, actually brings in, and answers that it brings in everything. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With כלל ופרט וכלל, only items similar to the details were included. With ריבה ומיעט וריבה, almost everything is included, so the scope of כפל becomes very wide.

keyTerms.meaning: included; the wording widens the law

phrases.english: What does it include?
phrases.notes: "It" is the doubled words ״המצא תמצא״, now read as including something extra.

phrases.english: Does it include all things?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the result of adopting ריבה ומיעט וריבה from Step 9–10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is included by ריבה ומיעט וריבה here?

steps.title: Then why list all the details?
steps.stepSummary: If everything is included, the animal details seem pointless.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need all these details?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If the פסוק includes everything, why does it bother naming שור, חמור and שה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The details must teach something. If the general words already cover everything, the listed animals look extra, and the תורה does not write extra words.

keyTerms.meaning: the details, the specific items listed

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, כֹּל הָנֵי פְּרָטֵי לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need all these details?
phrases.notes: The details are ox, donkey and sheep in the פסוק (שמות 22:3).

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, כֹּל הָנֵי פְּרָטֵי לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 11's conclusion that everything is included.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ריבה ומיעט וריבה includes everything
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If everything is included, the specific animal words have no job.

steps.title: Each detail excludes one thing
steps.stepSummary: The three animal details exclude land, slaves and documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: One excludes land, one excludes slaves, and one excludes documents.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each detail has a job. Each one removes one category from כפל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ריבה ומיעט וריבה, the details do not limit the law to things like themselves. They only take out a few items. The three details take out three things: קרקע, עבדים and שטרות.
steps.whatToRemember: Under ריבה ומיעט וריבה, everything gets כפל except land, slaves and documents.

phrases.english: One is to exclude land,
and one is to exclude slaves,
and one is to exclude documents.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by giving each detail a job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns a separate exclusion to each detail
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The details are extra once everything is included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each detail excludes one category: land, slaves, documents.

steps.title: ״גניבה״ and ״חיים״ teach רב's rule
steps.stepSummary: The words ״גניבה״ and ״חיים״ teach that the thief pays the value the item had when he stole it.
steps.simpleTranslation: ״Theft″ and ״alive″ come for רב's rule: he must restore the principal to what it was when he stole it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the words ״גניבה״ and ״חיים״ do now that they are no longer part of a כלל ופרט וכלל. They teach רב's rule about how much the thief pays back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, ״חיים״ was treated as the last generalization (Steps 2–3) and as the source for including animals (Step 6). Now that it is not needed for that, it teaches that the stolen item is treated as still ״alive″, at the value it had at the time of theft. So if the item lost value later, the thief still pays the original value.

keyTerms.meaning: "revive" the principal; pay its full original value
the principal, the basic value of the stolen item
as it was when he stole it

phrases.english: ״Theft″ and ״alive″
phrases.notes: Both words are from שמות 22:3: ״הגנבה... חיים″.

phrases.english: are for the rule of רב, who says:
He must revive the principal, as it was when he stole it.
phrases.notes: The word ״אחייה″ (revive) plays on ״חיים″ (alive).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ריבה ומיעט וריבה reading by giving the remaining words a job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns leftover words to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״גניבה″ and ״חיים″ would have no job once the reading changed.
steps.terutzMaskana: They teach רב's rule: the thief pays the value at the time of theft.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for a basic rule of theft: the thief's payment is fixed at the item's value when it was stolen.

steps.title: The other view: what does ״אם המצא תמצא״ teach?
steps.stepSummary: For the view that one פסוק is about a real thief, ״אם המצא תמצא״ is not needed for the thief's כפל, so what does it teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says one פסוק is about a thief and one is about someone who falsely claims a thief took it, and he learns the thief's own payment from ״if the thief shall be found″, what does he learn from ״אם המצא תמצא″?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now switches to a different opinion about the two פסוקים of the שומר. It asks what ״אם המצא תמצא״ teaches according to that opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the real thief's כפל came from ״אם המצא תמצא״. But this other opinion learns the thief's כפל from ״אם ימצא הגנב״. So ״אם המצא תמצא״ seems to have no job.

keyTerms.meaning: a שומר who falsely claims a thief stole the item

steps.confusionAlert: Steps 1–14 followed the view that both פסוקים are about a lying שומר. This step starts a different view, where one פסוק is about a real thief.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says one is about a thief
and one is about one who claims a thief's claim,
phrases.notes: That's a שומר who says "a thief took it," but he's lying.

phrases.english: and he learns the thief himself
from ״if the thief shall be found″,
phrases.notes: שמות 22:6

phrases.english: this ״if it shall be found″
phrases.notes: שמות 22:3

phrases.english: what does he learn from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר חַד בְּגַנָּב וְחַד בְּטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the view analyzed so far and asks about a different view of the two פסוקים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What ״אם המצא תמצא″ teaches for the view that learns the thief's כפל from ״אם ימצא הגנב″.

steps.title: It teaches that one who admits to a fine is exempt
steps.stepSummary: ״אם המצא תמצא״ teaches רבא בר אהילאי's source for רב: one who admits to a קנס is exempt, even if witnesses come later.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for רבא בר אהילאי's teaching. רבא בר אהילאי said: What is the reason of רב, who says that one who admits to a fine and afterward witnesses come is exempt? Because it is written ״אם המצא תמצא″: if it is found through witnesses, it will be found by judges. This leaves out one who makes himself guilty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״אם המצא תמצא״ is used for a different law. A person pays a fine only when witnesses prove it, not when he admits it on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The doubled word is split in two: the first ״found″ means through witnesses, the second ״found″ means by judges. So a fine is paid only when witnesses bring it to court. If he admitted first, he is exempt, even if witnesses came afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: a fine; a payment beyond the actual loss, like כפל
one who admits he owes a fine
one who makes himself guilty by his own admission

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a major rule across all fines: מודה בקנס פטור. A person's own admission cannot make him pay a קנס.

phrases.english: He needs it for the teaching of רבא בר אהילאי,
as רבא בר אהילאי said:
What is the reason of רב, who said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדֶה בִּקְנָס וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּאוּ עֵדִים – פָּטוּר?
phrases.english: One who admits to a fine, and afterward witnesses came, is exempt?
As it is written: ״If it shall be found″
if it is found through witnesses,
it will be found by judges;
this excludes one who makes himself guilty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15 by giving ״אם המצא תמצא″ a new job.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the source that one who admits to a קנס is exempt, even if witnesses later come.

steps.title: The both-שומר view: where is the admission rule from?
steps.stepSummary: For the view that both פסוקים are about a lying שומר, ״אם המצא תמצא״ is used for the thief, so where does the admission exemption come from?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says both are about someone who claims a thief took it, who uses ״אם המצא תמצא″ for the thief himself, where do we learn that one who makes himself guilty is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks about the view it followed earlier. There, ״אם המצא תמצא״ is busy teaching the thief's own כפל, so it cannot also teach the admission rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each view must have a source for מודה בקנס פטור. Since this view already uses ״אם המצא תמצא״ for the thief, it needs a different פסוק.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says both
are about one who claims a thief's claim,
so that this ״if it shall be found″
he applies to the thief himself,
from where do we know about one who makes himself guilty?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בְּטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the view used in Steps 1–14 to supply the source given in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the admission exemption according to the view that both פסוקים are about a lying שומר.

steps.title: The source is ״אשר ירשיען אלהים״
steps.stepSummary: This view learns the admission exemption from ״אשר ירשיען אלהים״: only the one whom judges convict pays, not one who convicts himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: From ״the one whom the judges convict″, and not the one who makes himself guilty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this view learns the rule from a different פסוק. The person pays כפל only when the judges find him guilty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אשר ירשיען אלהים״ says the judges make him guilty. If he made himself guilty by admitting, it is not the judges who convicted him, so he does not pay the fine. Both views agree on this basic exemption. Steps 19–21 show they still differ when witnesses come after the admission.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views agree that one who admits to a קנס, with no witnesses ever coming, is exempt. They use different sources: ״אם המצא תמצא״ or ״אשר ירשיען אלהים״. As step 21 shows, they disagree when witnesses come later.

phrases.english: From ״the one whom the judges convict″
phrases.notes: שמות 22:8. Here ״אלהים״ means the judges, not God.

phrases.english: and not one who makes himself guilty.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵ״אֲשֶׁר יַרְשִׁיעֻן אֱלֹהִים״ – וְלֹא הַמַּרְשִׁיעַ אֶת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17 with a different פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The exemption comes from ״אשר ירשיען אלהים″: only one convicted by judges pays.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Every view has a source for the basic rule מודה בקנס פטור, though they use different פסוקים.

steps.title: What does ״אשר ירשיען״ teach for the split view?
steps.stepSummary: For the view that one פסוק is about a real thief and one is about a lying שומר, the self-incrimination exemption comes from ״אם המצא תמצא״, so what is ״אשר ירשיען״ for?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says one פסוק is about a thief and one is about someone who falsely claims a thief stole it, who learns from ״אם המצא תמצא״ that one who incriminates himself is exempt, what does he learn from ״אשר ירשיען״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the question from step 17. Now it asks the other opinion what it does with the words ״אשר ירשיען״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 18 the both-שומר view used ״אשר ירשיען״ for the admission exemption. The split view already gets that exemption from ״אם המצא תמצא״, so ״אשר ירשיען״ seems to have no job for it.

keyTerms.meaning: A שומר who falsely claims that a thief stole the item
One who makes himself guilty, by his own admission
What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And according to the one who says one is about a thief
and one is about one who claims a thief's claim,
phrases.notes: This means a שומר who lies and says a thief stole the item.

phrases.english: who brings it from ״if it shall surely be found״
for one who incriminates himself,
this ״whom the judges convict״, what does he learn from it?
phrases.notes: שמות 22:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror question to step 17, now asked of the split view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of ״אשר ירשיען״ for the split view

steps.title: ״אשר ירשיען״ teaches the basic admission exemption
steps.stepSummary: The split view uses ״אשר ירשיען״ for the basic rule that one who admits to a קנס is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He can tell you: that פסוק is needed to teach that one who admits to a קנס is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that ״אשר ירשיען״ teaches the simple rule: if you admit to a קנס, you do not pay it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the split view uses two sources for two levels. ״אשר ירשיען״ teaches the basic exemption for one who admits. ״אם המצא תמצא״ adds that he stays exempt even if witnesses come later.

keyTerms.meaning: One who admits that he owes a fine
Exempt, does not have to pay
It is needed for him to teach

phrases.english: He can say to you:
that one is needed for him
for one who admits to a fine, that he is exempt.
phrases.notes: Here this means when no witnesses ever come. The later-witnesses case comes from ״אם המצא תמצא״.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמוֹדֶה בִּקְנָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״אשר ירשיען״ teaches that one who admits to a קנס is exempt when no witnesses come; ״אם המצא תמצא״ extends this to when witnesses come later

steps.title: The both-שומר view must disagree with רבא בר אהילאי's teaching for רב
steps.stepSummary: The view that both פסוקים are about a lying שומר holds that one who admits to a קנס and then witnesses come is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says both are about one who claims a thief's claim holds: one who admits to a fine and afterward witnesses came is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what follows for the both-שומר view. It has no extra פסוק left for the later-witnesses rule, so it must say he does pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view uses ״אם המצא תמצא״ for the thief and ״אשר ירשיען״ for the basic admission exemption. No source is left for רב's rule from step 16, so this view rules the opposite: once witnesses come, he pays the קנס.
steps.whatToRemember: The two views split on a practical question. The split view says one who admits to a קנס is exempt even if witnesses come later. The both-שומר view says he becomes liable once witnesses come.

phrases.english: And the one who says both of them
are about one who claims a thief's claim,
holds: one who admits to a fine
and afterward witnesses came is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר תַּרְוַיְיהוּ בְּטוֹעֵן טַעֲנַת גַּנָּב, קָסָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic result of the both-שומר view's use of the פסוקים in steps 17-18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the both-שומר view, one who admits to a קנס and is later proven guilty by witnesses must pay

steps.title: Why does the split view need all the details in the first פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: For the split view, the thief's law comes from the later פסוק, so why does the first פסוק list ox, donkey, sheep and alive?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says one is about a thief and one is about one who claims a thief's claim, who learns the thief from there: granted, ״אם המצא תמצא״ is for רבא בר אהילאי's teaching. But all these details, why do I need them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the split view again. One phrase has a job, but the rest of the פסוק's details seem to have none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The split view learns the thief's כפל from the other פסוק, and ״אם המצא תמצא״ goes to רבא בר אהילאי. The list of ox, donkey, sheep and alive now seems extra, because it only matters for the thief's law, which comes from somewhere else.

phrases.english: And according to the one who says one is about a thief
and one is about one who claims a thief's claim,
who learns the thief from there;
phrases.notes: "From there" means the other פסוק, the one about a real thief (שמות 22:6).

phrases.english: granted, ״if it shall surely be found״
is for the teaching of רבא בר אהילאי.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל כֹּל הָנֵי פְּרָטֵי, לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: But all these details, why do I need them?
phrases.notes: He means ox, donkey, sheep and ״alive״ in שמות 22:3.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל כֹּל הָנֵי פְּרָטֵי, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the phrase ״אשר ירשיען״ to the remaining details of the first פסוק under the split view
steps.kashyaTarget: The split view's reading of the first פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the thief's law comes from the later פסוק, the details that define the thief's law in the first פסוק seem to teach nothing

steps.title: A repeated passage is repeated for one new point
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught that the תורה may repeat a whole passage just for the sake of one new detail.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: any passage that was said and then repeated was only repeated for a new thing introduced in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the extra details do not need their own lesson. The whole passage is repeated just to teach one new point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק repeats the thief's law already found elsewhere. It is repeated only for its one new point, ״אם המצא תמצא״ (רבא בר אהילאי's rule). The other details come along as part of the repeated passage.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל
A new thing introduced in it

steps.whatToRemember: A passage the תורה repeats may be there for just one new detail, and the other words need not each teach something.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not look for a separate lesson in each of ox, donkey, sheep and alive here. The answer is that they have none of their own under this view; only the one new detail matters.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule from the school of רבי ישמעאל is used across the תורה to explain why some passages seem to repeat themselves.

phrases.english: Like the school of רבי ישמעאל taught
for the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
any passage that was said and then repeated,
was only repeated
for a thing that is new in it.
phrases.notes: The new thing here is ״אם המצא תמצא״, which teaches רבא בר אהילאי's rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: General rule of reading the תורה: a repeated passage exists for its one new point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each detail in the first פסוק must teach its own lesson, and under the split view they teach nothing
steps.terutzMaskana: The whole passage is repeated for ״אם המצא תמצא״; the other details are simply part of the repetition

steps.title: Maybe a thief also pays double only after an oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that a real thief, like the lying שומר, should pay double only if he swore falsely.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that a thief himself pays double only when he swore falsely!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. Since the thief and the lying שומר are taught near each other, maybe the oath condition of the שומר also applies to the thief.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lying שומר pays double only if he swears falsely that the item was stolen. If the two cases are linked, maybe the thief also needs a false oath before he pays כפל. This would make the thief's כפל much narrower.

keyTerms.meaning: The actual thief himself, not a שומר who claims there was a thief
With an oath; here, a false oath denying the theft
'But say...'; introduces a proposed alternative reading

phrases.english: But say that a thief himself
pays double only with an oath!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the link between the thief and the שומר discussed in the previous steps and suggests carrying the oath condition over to the thief.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that a real thief pays כפל with no oath condition.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the thief and the lying שומר sit side by side, the oath condition of the שומר should apply to the thief as well.

steps.title: רבי יעקב teaches that a thief pays double even without an oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion with a ברייתא: 'he shall pay double' means even without an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: That can't be, since a ברייתא teaches: רבי יעקב says, 'he shall pay double' means even without an oath. Do you say without an oath, or only with an oath? You must say it was not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the idea is wrong and brings a ברייתא of רבי יעקב. He reads 'he shall pay double' as covering a thief who never swore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב states the rule and then asks himself whether the פסוק might mean only with an oath. He rejects that with 'it was not so', but he does not yet explain why. The next step will ask what that phrase means.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It can't enter your mind'; the idea is rejected
'He shall pay double'; the words of the פסוק about the thief
The תנא who teaches this ברייתא

phrases.english: That can't enter your mind;
as it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Ya'akov says:
"He shall pay double" means even without an oath.
phrases.notes: שמות 22:3, the פסוק about the real thief.

phrases.english: Do you say it means without an oath,
or does it mean only with an oath?
You must say: it was not so.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ; דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24 by citing a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Citing a ברייתא that reads the פסוק against the suggestion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thief, like the שומר, pays double only with an oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: A thief pays double even without an oath.

steps.title: What does 'it was not so' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יעקב proved that the פסוק can't mean 'only with an oath'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'it was not so'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבי יעקב's short rejection. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יעקב only said 'it was not so' without giving a proof. The גמרא wants to know what logic rules out the oath reading.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was not so'; רבי יעקב's short rejection of the oath reading

phrases.english: What is meant by "it was not so"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ברייתא's last phrase.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The proof that the פסוק can't be limited to a thief who swore.

steps.title: אביי: a thief with an oath could be learned by קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that if the thief paid double only with an oath, it would already follow by קל וחומר from the lying שומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Let the תורה not write 'he shall pay double' about a thief, and let it come by קל וחומר from the one who claims a thief took it. If the שומר, who got the item in a permitted way, pays double, then surely the thief, who got it in a forbidden way, does too!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question. He shows that a thief who swore falsely would not need his own פסוק, since a קל וחומר from the lying שומר would already teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The lying שומר received the item properly, yet if he swears falsely he pays double. The thief took it wrongly from the start, so he is surely worse. So a thief who swore falsely would already be covered by the קל וחומר without any פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
A שומר who falsely claims that a thief stole the item
'The Merciful One'; a name for ה׳ as giver of the תורה

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Let the Merciful One not write "he shall pay double" about a thief,
and let it come through a kal vachomer
from the one who claims a thief took it:
phrases.notes: This is the lying שומר, who says 'it was stolen' when he really kept it.

phrases.english: If the one who claims a thief took it,
who got the item into his hands in a permitted way,
the פסוק says he pays double;
then a thief himself, who got it into his hands in a forbidden way,
isn't it all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא ״שְׁנַיִם יְשַׁלֵּם״ בְּגַנָּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26 by showing that the oath reading would make the thief's פסוק unnecessary.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A thief who swore falsely would already pay double by קל וחומר from the lying שומר, so the פסוק can't be talking only about that case.

steps.title: So the thief's פסוק teaches double payment even without an oath
steps.stepSummary: Since the קל וחומר already covers a thief who swore, the extra words teach that a thief pays double even without an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why do I need 'he shall pay double' written about the thief himself? To teach that he pays even without an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his point. The תורה's words about the thief must teach something new: double payment even with no oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the קל וחומר already teaches the oath case, the פסוק about the thief would be extra if it meant only that. So it must widen the rule to a thief who never swore. This backs up רבי יעקב and answers the challenge of step 24.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Why do I need it?'; asks what an extra phrase in the פסוק teaches
'That even'; introduces the new thing the פסוק adds

steps.whatToRemember: A real thief pays כפל even without an oath. If the thief's פסוק were only about a thief who swore, it would be unneeded, because a קל וחומר from the lying שומר already teaches that.

phrases.english: Rather, "he shall pay double"
that the Merciful One wrote about the thief himself,
why do I need it?
To teach that he pays even without an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא ״שְׁנַיִם יְשַׁלֵּם״ דִּכְתַב רַחֲמָנָא בְּגַנָּב עַצְמוֹ, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from אביי's קל וחומר and explains רבי יעקב's 'it was not so'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The thief's פסוק teaches that a thief pays double even without a false oath, so the suggestion of step 24 is rejected.

steps.title: Are the words 'if it shall be found' already needed for something else?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the derivation from 'אם המצא' by pointing out that a ברייתא needs this פסוק for a different lesson, beginning with the word 'ידו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does this phrase, 'if it shall be found,' really come to teach this? But it is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: 'his hand'...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion it just reached. It says the words 'אם המצא' seem to be needed for a different lesson taught in a ברייתא, and it starts quoting that ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that extra words in the פסוק teach that a גנב pays כפל without an oath. A teaching can only come from words that are not already used for another lesson. Here the גמרא argues that the same פסוק is already used by a ברייתא, so it may not be free to teach our point. The ברייתא's content starts with 'ידו' and continues in the next part.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If it shall be found': the words in the פסוק about a thief that were just used to teach double payment without an oath
'Does it come for this?' A challenge asking whether a פסוק really teaches the point just made
'It is needed for': the words are already used for another teaching
'As was taught in a ברייתא': introduces a ברייתא as the source
'His hand': the word from the same פסוק that the ברייתא explains

steps.confusionAlert: The quote stops at 'ידו' because the ברייתא is only starting here. Its lesson comes next. Do not think 'ידו' alone is the whole challenge.

phrases.english: And this phrase, "if it shall be found"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:3

phrases.english: does it come for this purpose?
But it is needed
for that which was taught in a ברייתא: "his hand"
phrases.notes: This is the start of the ברייתא. It explains the word 'his hand' from the same פסוק, and the explanation continues next.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי אִם הִמָּצֵא לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא הָא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source used in the conclusion of Step 28 by claiming the פסוק is already used for another lesson.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation that 'אם המצא' teaches that a גנב pays כפל even without an oath.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק that is already needed for one teaching cannot also be used for another. A ברייתא uses this פסוק (starting with 'ידו') for a different lesson, so it may not be free for this one.
